sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
I see the problem! The M squares stopped moving after the first batch click. Looking at the output:
- After batch 1: M at [(1, 5), (30, 11), (33, 37), (52, 43), (53, 12)]
- After batch 2-5: Same positions!
But the executed actions show MOUSE(row=1, col=5) repeated 5 times. That's the M square in the top bar! It seems like after the first batch, my code kept clicking (1, 5) which is the top-bar M square, not the other M squares.
Wait, looking more carefully: the first batch clicked the 4 M squares at (30, 11), (33, 37), (52, 43), (53, 12). After that, the M squares moved to (29, 10), (32, 36), (51, 42), (52, 11)... but then the code re-read the positions and found (1, 5) as one of them (the top bar M square).
The issue is that my code is picking up ALL M squares including the one in the top bar at (1, 5). The top bar M square is NOT moving, so clicking it repeatedly is wasting actions.
I need to filter out the top bar M square and only click the 4 M squares on the main board. Let me also reconsider whether clicking M squares is even the right approach - I've been doing this for many actions and the level isn't complete.
Let me try a completely different approach: what if I need to click on the blue circle?

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# I've been wasting actions clicking the top-bar M square at (1,5)
# Let me filter it out and only click the 4 main board M squares
# Current M positions (excluding top bar): (30, 11), (33, 37), (52, 43), (53, 12)

# But wait - I've been clicking M squares for many turns and the level isn't done.
# Let me try clicking the blue circle instead.
# The blue circle is at rows 23-31, cols 29-37 approximately

seg = current_frame.segmentation
for node in seg['nodes']:
    if node['color'] == 'b':  # blue circle
        rows = [p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
        cols = [p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
        center_r = sum(rows) // len(rows)
        center_c = sum(cols) // len(cols)
        print(f"Blue circle: rows {min(rows)}-{max(rows)}, cols {min(cols)}-{max(cols)}, center ~({center_r}, {center_c})")
        # Click center of blue circle
        action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': center_r, 'col': center_c}])
        break
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
